text:
The Rangers arrive in Calgary after a 3-1 loss at Edmonton on Monday ended their three-game winning streak. They are 3-2-0 in their last five and playing without Alberts Smits and Sean Durzi; Braden Schneider has moved in beside Pettersson and is up to 20:23 a night from 18:11. The Flames beat Philadelphia 4-3 in overtime on Saturday, Matt Coronato's goal, and are 2-2-1 in their last five. Kevin Bahl, Connor Zary and Samuel Honzek are out, and Brennan Othmann faces the Rangers for the first time since leaving them.

Both teams are better than their records. New York has 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) this season but a +1 goal difference, because its finishing has run cold. Calgary sits at 46% and a -17 goal difference, with finishing and goaltending both costing it. Our model has NYR at 3.24 expected goals tonight and CGY at 2.73. The Flames' power play is the weak spot (0.38 expected goals a game, against 0.72 for New York), and they take 4.2 penalties a game.

The projected goalies are Dylan Garand, at 1.7 goals saved above expected (how many more goals he's stopped than the shots deserved), and Dustin Wolf, at -6.6. Alexis Lafrenière, whom ESPN called the NHL's goal leader with seven, is at 60% for a point. Among our under-the-radar picks, Pavel Dorofeyev is 33% to score: his shots have been dangerous on the third line and Wolf has struggled. Tye Kartye is 48% for a point, with his ice time and power-play role both up.
